r13792: EO 13792 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act, signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13792.txt, OCR text layer of three PDF pages; page images were not inspected and requires_page_check is false). Operative content: Sec. 1 policy; Sec. 2(a)-(c) Secretary of the Interior review of monument designations, factors and consultation; Sec. 2(d)-(e) interim report in 45 days and final report in 120 days (report deadlines, never ends); Sec. 3 general provisions. It has no sunset and no own-terms ending. The first and only end found is Sec. 7(a) of EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037; held official text, Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 read in full): 'Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act) ... are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 13792 is unconditional (the exception wording in Sec. 7 concerns only EO 13834, EO 13920 and memoranda) and EO 13990 states no delayed effective date, so it took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR catalog: 2 hits, both EO 13990, no reinstatement candidate) were read and carry no coverage warning; they show no earlier ending and no later revival. Judgment on performance: the Secretary's review and reports ordered by Sec. 2 may have been completed in 2017, but no held source dates them, a report deadline is not an end and the order is not self-terminating, so the order is treated as operative until revoked on 2021-01-20. The independent reviewer should test that judgment.
r10192: EO 10192 (December 15, 1950, 15 FR 9029) was read in the held official Federal Register extract (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10192.txt, 19,424 chars). The order is only the two numbered amendments at about chars 15,127-15,308; the rest of the extract is neighbouring Federal Register material including EO 10193. It amends EO 10129 of June 3, 1950 (President's Commission on Migratory Labor, held): para 1 changes the paragraph 3 report date from 'December 15, 1950' to 'March 1, 1951'; para 2 changes 'Thirty days' to 'Sixty days' in paragraph 8 (EO 10129 para 8 as issued: 'Thirty days after rendition of its report to the President, the Commission shall cease to exist unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order'). The first end is EO 10236 (signed 1951-04-26, 16 FR 3607; held official text): 'paragraph 8 ... as amended by paragraph 2 of Executive Order No. 10192 ... be, and it is hereby, further amended to read as follows: "8. The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31, 1951."' Clause 2 (the 'Sixty days' wording) was replaced on 1951-04-26; clause 1 (the changed report date) was spent when the Commission ceased to exist at the end of 1951-05-31, which is also the whole-order end. A report deadline is not an end and the actual report date is not held, so I treated the amendment of a deadline as ending with the body whose report it governed; the independent reviewer should test that choice. The machine searches (usc 0 hits, ecfr 0 hits, OFR catalog 1 hit) carry no coverage warning; the single catalog hit points at EO 10263 only because of a mis-attributed date and is resolved above.
r10999: EO 10999 (Assigning Emergency Preparedness Functions to the Secretary of Commerce, signed 1962-02-16, 27 FR 1527-1532) was read in full from the held official Federal Register extract (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10999.txt, 24,413 chars; page images not inspected). The extract begins with the tail of EO 10998 (Agriculture, Secs. 8-12) and ends with the opening of EO 11000 (Labor); neither is part of EO 10999. The machine draft inventory had 46 records with duplicated sub-items that mixed those neighbours, so I replaced it with the 13 sections of EO 10999 (Secs. 1-13) using absolute character spans in the held file. EO 10999 has no sunset. Its first end is EO 11490 (signed 1969-10-28, 34 FR 17567): Sec. 3015 'The following are hereby revoked:' lists '(7) Executive Order No. 10999 of February 16, 1962' (official Federal Register text jobs/family-rule-tail/output/texts/EO_11490_tail.txt, and the APP transcription); the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note independently records that EO 10999 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 11490, Oct. 28, 1969, 34 F.R. 17567'. EO 11490 states no effective date or delay, so it took effect on signing, 1969-10-28. Sec. 3014 (retention of existing authority) is expressly 'except as provided by Section 3015' and so does not save EO 10999. Search scope: current-law:usc (one editorial note stating the revocation), current-law:ecfr (no section in the eCFR search hits lists EO 10999), later-events:ofr_catalog (all hits are EO 11490); none has a coverage warning. The dossier's missing item (EO 10952, a Department of Defense order named in Sec. 6) is only a cross-reference and is not an acting instrument for EO 10999.
